summary: Petition under Regulations 10 & 18 of CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 for the grant of a Renewable Energy Certificate. **Parties Present:** Shri S Vallinayagam, Advocate, PCKL Shri Gajendra Sinh Vasava, NLDC The Petitioner, Power Company of Karnataka Limited (PCKL), is a Government Company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956, and is acting on behalf of the Distribution Companies of Karnataka, viz. Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Ltd (BESCOM), Mangalore Electricity Supply Company Ltd (MESCOM), Hubli Electricity Supply Company Ltd (HESCOM), Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company Ltd (GESCOM), Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Ltd (CESC) regarding power purchase activities. 3. The Petitioner, PCKL, has filed the present Petition under Regulations 10 and 18 of the REC Regulations, 2022, seeking relaxation of the timeline prescribed under Regulation 10(3) for submission of applications to the Respondent, NLDC, for issuance of RECs in respect of the surplus Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) achieved by HESCOM and GESCOM during FY 2023-24. - _(a) Exercise its power conferred under Regulation 18 and relax the period allowed for submission of the application for RE Certificate for the period of 2023-2024._ - _(b) Consequently, direct the Central Agency to accept the applications of HESCOM and GESCOM for the issuance of REC._ - _(c) Pass any other order or orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case_ - (e) Upon receiving all required documents from the respective departments, HESCOM submitted to NLDC on July 25, 2025, requesting the issuance of RECs for FY 23-24. - (f) The subsequent submission of supporting documents in July 2025 was delayed due to the late issuance of the mandatory recommendations by KERC and SLDC, which was beyond HESCOM's control. copies of all documents on August 12, 2025, requesting the issuance of RECs for FY 23-24. - (n) The subsequent submission of supporting documents in August 2025 was delayed due to the late issuance of the mandatory recommendations by KERC and SLDC, which was beyond GESCOM's control. - (q) Also, CERC proposed the REC (First Amendment) Regulations, 2025 and proposed the amendment to Regulation 10 of the Principal Regulation. - (r) Accordingly, the Petitioner requested the Commission to exercise “power to relax” as it will not adversely affect anyone, nor will it be a precedent, because of the factual position in the present application. 2. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking relaxation of the period allowed for submission of the application for RECs for the FY 2023-24 and the consequent direction to the Central Agency to accept the application of HESCOM and GSCOM for the issuance of RECs. After hearing the matter, the Commission admitted the petition and issued notice to the Respondent. The Commission also directed the Respondent to file its reply and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any. 3. During the course of the hearing, no one was present on behalf of the Petitioner when the matter was called out. The Respondent's representative submitted that NLDC has no objection to the Petition. In view of the above, the Commission, while permitting the Petitioner to file its written submissions, if any, within 10 days, reserved the matter for order. 4. The Commission has heard the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondent and has carefully perused the records. 6. In view of the above, the only issue that arises for consideration is **_ whether the timeline prescribed under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations, 2022 may be relaxed for issuance of RECs to HESCOM and GESCOM under Regulation 18 of the REC Regulations, 2022 _ .** _The Commission may, from time to time, issue such practice directions and orders as considered appropriate for the implementation of these regulations_ _The Commission may by general or special order, for reasons to be recorded in writing, and after giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties likely to be affected, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by interested person(s)._ 10. As per the principle laid down for the grant of RECs, the Petitioner is an eligible entity being a distribution licensee, and it will be entitled to RECs subject to the fulfilment of 11. In our view, the delay in the application for issuance of the REC is procedural in nature due to the reasons stated by the Petitioner and is not likely to prejudice any of the stakeholders, including the Respondent. Accordingly, the timelines stipulated under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations 2022 are hereby relaxed, and the Petitioner is permitted to file its application for the issuance of RECs before the Central Agency for FY 2023-24. 12. Accordingly, the Respondent, NLDC, is directed to issue the RECs for FY 2023-24 to the Petitioner, PCKL, after due verification and satisfying itself that the Petitioner meets all other conditions and has submitted all the required documents for the issuance of RECs.
title: Petition under Regulations 10 & 18 of CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 for the grant of a Renewable Energy Certificate. Power Company of Karnataka Limited
